marks.gloss_en: איבעיא להו: אוממות או עוממות? תא שמע דאמר רב חסדא בר אבדימי: ארזים לא עממהו בגן אלהים
Rav Chisda bar Avdimi said [the verse]: 'the cedars in the garden of God could not dim it' (Ezek 31:8)
כיון דשמענא להא דרב יהודה אמר רב, אנא נמי לא מהדרנא -- since I heard Rav's dictum, I too do not seek out fire
Rav: one does not seek out fire the way one seeks out mitzvot
Rav: the mishnah's 'until they benefit' is not literal benefit, but any flame such that, were he standing near, he could use its light -- even at a distance
over glowing coals one blesses
Rava: 'until they benefit' means actual benefit from the light
Ulla: [the benefit is light] enough to tell an issar from a pundeyon
Rav Yehuda would bless over [the light of] the house of Adda the servant
Rav Zevid: the dispute [of Beit Shammai and Beit Hillel over one who ate and did not bless] is where he forgot
תדע -- the gulyarin open the battle and the mighty win it
R' Nehorai: know it -- the gulyarin go down and open the battle, and the mighty go down and win
דתניא: ...אלא שממהרין למברך יותר מן העונה אמן -- a tanna holds the one who blesses is preferred
תנאי היא -- it is a tannaitic dispute: another baraita has them hasten to the one who blesses more
the baraita: both the one who blesses and the one who answers amen are included, but they hasten to the one who blesses more than to the one who answers amen
כשם שמזוהם פסול לעבודה, כך ידים מזוהמות פסולות לברכה
R' Zilai: oil holds back the blessing
וכי לא שמע היכי נפיק? -- if he did not hear [the whole blessing], how does he discharge [his obligation]?
the stam's inference: after an Israelite, one answers amen even though he did not hear the whole blessing
בשלא אכל עמהן -- the case is one who did not eat with them, and so is not discharging an obligation (= p_beshelo_achal)
Chiyya bar Rav: [the mishnah speaks of one] who did not eat with them
והתניא רבי יוסי אומר: גדול העונה אמן יותר מן המברך -- a baraita says the reverse
the stam's inference: the one who blesses is preferable to the one who answers amen
Rav: after everyone one answers amen, except schoolchildren
Rav Nachman bar Yitzchak: I know neither Zilai nor Zivai nor Zuhamai; I know a teaching
for his own honour (a forgotten purse) he goes back up the Bira; for the honour of Heaven (a forgotten blessing), all the more so
one goes back up for a forgotten purse -- the lenient side of the kal vachomer
לדבריכם, מי שאכל בראש הבירה ושכח וירד ולא בירך, יחזור לראש הבירה ויברך?! -- by your words he must climb back up the Temple Mount to bless?!
לדבריכם, מי ששכח ארנקי בראש הבירה לא יעלה ויטלנה? לכבוד עצמו הוא עולה, לכבוד שמים לא כל שכן?! (= kv_kavod_shamayim, from p_arnaki_oleh)
Beit Hillel to Beit Shammai: by your words, one who ate atop the Bira, forgot, and descended without blessing must go back up to the top of the Bira and bless?!
ושכח תנן -- the mishnah's case is one who forgot
you might have said: the same [Beit Hillel's ruling] holds even where he did it deliberately
one student, [who had not blessed] unwittingly, did as Beit Shammai and found a purse of gold
Rabba bar bar Chana was travelling in a caravan; he ate, forgot, and did not bless
why a dove? because the community of Israel is likened to a dove
מי אמר ריש לקיש הכי? והאמר רב אמי אמר ריש לקיש: כדי להלך ארבע מילין! -- did Reish Lakish say thirst? Rav Ami reports him saying four mil
Rav Ami in Reish Lakish's name: the measure of digestion is the time it takes to walk four mil
לא קשיא: כאן באכילה מרובה, כאן באכילה מועטת -- the two measures are for a large and a small meal (= p_kan_meruba, p_kan_muetet)
here [the four mil] -- with a large meal (the pairing is Steinsaltz's)
R' Yochanan: [digestion lasts] as long as he is not hungry

מיתיבי... ראה שלהבת ולא נשתמש לאורה -- אינו מברך; (53b.4) בשלמא נשתמש לאורה ולא ראה שלהבת משכחת לה דקיימא בקרן זוית, אלא ראה שלהבת ולא נשתמש לאורה היכי משכחת לה? לאו דמרחקא?! -- the case of seeing without using must be a distance, and there he does not bless

if his candle was hidden in his lap or in a lantern, or he saw the flame and did not use its light, or used its light and did not see the flame -- he does not bless until he both sees the flame and uses its light
לא, כגון דעמיא ואזלא -- no: as where it is dimming away
